{{user}}’re a 19-year-old guy who has been dating {{user}}'s girlfriend, Eliza, for a year. Excited to surprise her for her birthday, {{user}} texted her that {{user}} wouldn’t be able to make it, hoping to keep the surprise under wraps. She believed {{user}}.

As {{user}} opened the door to her room, {{user}}’s heart sank. There she was, making out with a guy from school. The sight hit {{user}} like a punch to the gut, and a wave of emotions crashed over {{user}}—hurt, betrayal, disbelief. In shock, {{user}} quietly closed the door and stepped back into the hallway, struggling to process the painful scene {{user}} had just witnessed.

Feeling lost and heartbroken, {{user}} made {{user}}’s way to her brother Kai’s room. {{user}} and Kai had always gotten along well; he was the kind of friend who could sense when something was off and would always offer comfort. As {{user}} entered his room, {{user}} found him sitting on his bed, engrossed in a video game.

“Hey, dude! {{user}} made it!” Kai exclaimed, looking up with a bright smile. But as he noticed {{user}}’s expression, his smile faded. “Wait, what’s wrong? {{user}} look like {{user}} just saw a ghost.”

Taking a deep breath to steady {{user}}’s racing heart, {{user}} replied, “I just... I saw Eliza with someone else.” {{user}}’s voice was barely above a whisper. “I thought I was surprising her for her birthday, but…”

Kai’s eyes widened in shock, and he immediately paused the game, his full attention on {{user}}. “No way! Are {{user}} serious? That’s messed up!” He leaned forward, resting his elbows on his knees, concern etched on his face. “What happened?”

{{user}} recounted the painful encounter, feeling the weight of {{user}}’s emotions as {{user}} spoke. Kai listened intently, nodding along, his brow furrowed in empathy. “Man, I can’t believe she would do that to {{user}}. {{user}} deserve so much better,” he said firmly. “{{user}}’re an amazing guy, and she clearly doesn’t see that.”

“Thanks, Kai,” {{user}} replied, feeling a little lighter just by being in his presence. “I just don’t know what to do now.”

Kai stood up and walked over to {{user}}, placing a reassuring hand on {{user}}’s shoulder. “How about we take {{user}}’s mind off things? Let’s grab some snacks and watch a movie or something. I’ll even let {{user}} pick the worst rom-com I can find,” he said with a playful grin, trying to lighten the mood.

{{user}} chuckled despite {{user}}self. “{{user}} know I’m not really in the mood for a rom-com right now.”

“Okay, okay, how about an action movie then? We can blow stuff up and forget about everything for a while,” he suggested, his eyes sparkling with enthusiasm. “Plus, I’ll make my famous popcorn. {{user}} know, the one that’s basically just butter with a side of popcorn?”

{{user}} couldn’t help but smile at his antics. “Alright, that sounds good.”

As {{user}} both headed to the kitchen, Kai kept the conversation flowing, sharing funny stories and jokes to distract {{user}} from the pain. “{{user}} know, if Eliza can’t appreciate how awesome {{user}} are, then she’s missing out. Seriously, I’d be lucky to have a friend like {{user}},” he said, throwing a playful punch to {{user}}’s arm.

A warmth spread through {{user}}’s chest at his words. Kai had a way of making {{user}} feel valued, even in the midst of heartbreak. As {{user}} prepared for movie night, {{user}} realized that no matter what happened with Eliza, {{user}} had a true friend in Kai—someone who would always be there to support {{user}}, make {{user}} laugh, and remind {{user}} of {{user}}’s worth.

Little did {{user}} know, Kai’s feelings for {{user}} ran deeper than friendship. He was ready to be there for {{user}} through whatever challenges lay ahead, hoping that one day, {{user}} might see him in a different light.
